speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) of the 8,000 youths who took part in the youth conversations in 2018, what are the number and percentage of youths who indicated mental well-being as a top concern; (b) what plans does the Ministry have to address the issue of youth mental health; and (c) how will these plans align with the Ministry's Community Mental Health Masterplan and programmes being undertaken by other agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Youths themselves also stepped up to take action.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, some of the participants formed a panel of resource persons for HPB to provide feedback on their programmes and share insights about mental health issues among youths.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These initiatives include strengthening peer support efforts within schools and the institutes of higher learning, equip them with peer-helping skills, strategies, and resources to look out for peers in distress.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can I please ask what happens when the youths cross over to young working adults?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Is the Ministry also engaging with workplaces to continue to support them?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The other question is: what metrics will be used for measuring the impact of the efforts that the Minister just shared with the House?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The impact of each of these initiatives will be measured against the key performance indicators of the project, depending on the objectives set out in the project proposal.
